description: Volume capacity and latency per drive letter. Free % answers "will it fill up", latency and busy % answer "is it slow right now".

panels.description: Hosts where this collector failed its last scrape. Non-zero means the numbers on this page are incomplete - see the Collector scrape health row at the bottom.
panels.title: Scrape FAIL

panels.description: Volumes about to fill. A full system or SQL data volume takes the service down - clear space today.
panels.title: Free < 10%

panels.description: Warning band - plan the cleanup or the growth request.
panels.title: Free < 15%

panels.description: Volumes with average service time above 20ms. Users will notice on OLTP workloads.
panels.title: Latency > 20ms

panels.description: Severe storage latency. Check the physical disk / SAN path before blaming the application.
panels.title: Latency > 50ms

panels.description: Volumes with almost no idle time - saturated queues.
panels.title: Busy > 90%

panels.description: Worst volume in the selection.

panels.description: Volumes with the least idle time.

panels.description: One row per host + volume. Read and write latency are separated because write-back caches hide write latency while reads stay slow.

panels.description: Capacity action list. Absolute Free matters as much as the percentage on very large volumes.

panels.description: High latency with low IOPS means the storage itself is slow; high latency with high IOPS means you are simply asking for too much.

panels.description: Average seconds per I/O. Spikes that line up with a backup or index rebuild window are expected.

panels.description: Percentage of time the volume had at least one outstanding request.
panels.title: Busy % (topk 10)

panels.description: Bytes per second. Compare with the SAN or datastore limit before buying more disk.

panels.description: Operations per second - the number your storage team quotes limits in.

panels.description: Outstanding I/O. A persistently deep queue with high latency confirms saturation.

panels.description: Separates read queueing from write queueing when diagnosing a mixed workload.

panels.description: Same data as Free % from the other direction - handy for capacity reports.

panels.description: Capacity-oriented view for reporting and growth requests.

panels.description: Which volume is which. Useful when drive letters differ across hosts.

panels.description: FAIL rows mean every metric on this dashboard is stale for that host. Fix the exporter first, then re-read the KPIs.
panels.title: Scrape Health by Host

panels.description: Growing duration usually means the host is under load or the collector is querying more objects. Series capped with topk/bottomk to stay readable on a large fleet. Filter Server to see everything.
